turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Ag, doc, sorry to waste your time. It's just the big toe, a bit swollen, nothing hectic.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Howzit, Mr Pillay. Come through. Tell me properly what's going on with that toe.
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): The right one. It started this morning... no, shame, it was last night. I woke up and it was already sore.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Was it already swollen when you woke, or only once you were up and about?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Swollen when I woke. Looks like a balloon, but I'll be fine, hey.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Could you get a shoe on? How's the walking?
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): No shoe, I'm in slip-slops. It's sore to walk, throbbing a bit, but I'm not dying.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): If ten is the worst pain you've ever had, what number is this?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): A four... ag, no, I'm soft-pedalling. It's a seven. Throbbing. Still, it's not the end of the world.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever, chills, or feeling properly unwell with it?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): No. I'm not sick, no fever, nothing like that.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is any other joint sore, the ankle, the knee, the other foot?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): No. Just this one stupid toe. The rest is lekker.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you had this exact thing before?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): Once. I nearly said two years back, but no, it was a year back. Same toe, and it went away by itself.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long did that one last?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): Two or three days. I didn't bother coming in. It was nothing much.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any injury this time? A knock, a twist, something dropped on the foot?
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): No. No injury. I didn't kick anything, didn't drop a thing. It just came on.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): What are you drinking these days? Beer, wine, anything through the week?
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): I'm not a drinker. Weekends only. A beer or two at the braai, max.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): A beer or two as in two bottles, or a bit more than that when you're honest?
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): Eish, a six-pack of Castle on the Saturday. Sunday braai, maybe two more. Nothing in the week, I promise, and it's not a big deal.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): So a six-pack of Castle on Saturday, sometimes two extra at a Sunday braai, and dry through the week. That the size of it?
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): Ja. And half the guys at work drink way more, so don't look at me like that.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any medicines on the go? Prescribed, or from the chemist.
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): Only the water tablet, for my blood pressure. Nothing else.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): The name, and how much?
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): Hydrochlorothiazide. Fifty milligrams... ag, no, that's my brother's cholesterol pill, not mine. I take twenty-five milligrams, one every morning.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Every morning, or most mornings?
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): Every morning, with coffee. I don't skip.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Allergies to any medicine, or foods, or anything else?
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): No, none, never had one.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Let me look at the foot.
[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): Right big toe, where it joins the foot. You can touch it, it's not that bad.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): The base of the right big toe is hot, red and swollen, and it's markedly tender. Skin is intact. I can't see a bruise.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Blood pressure today is one hundred and forty-eight over ninety-two. Pulse is seventy-eight.
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): Ja, it always reads high in here. Anyway the parking was a proper mess, and load shedding flattened the bakkie battery last week, so I'm already irritated.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Parking's been chaos all month. Before we move on, anything else about how this started?
[SEG0040] person_1 (PATIENT): Oh. Wait. Yesterday afternoon I did kick the kitchen chair, barefoot. Tiny knock. I forgot because it was nothing.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Did the skin break, or did it swell up right then?
[SEG0042] person_1 (PATIENT): No break, and it didn't swell then. I carried on walking. Swelling only pitched up in the night, so the chair's got nothing to do with it.

[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me check I've got this straight: right big toe swollen and very sore since last night, no shoe, pain about seven out of ten, and the same thing a year ago for two or three days. You drink a six-pack of Castle on Saturdays, sometimes two more on a Sunday, and you take hydrochlorothiazide twenty-five milligrams every morning for blood pressure. Yesterday afternoon you knocked a chair barefoot, no cut, and it didn't swell until the night. Is that fair?
[SEG0044] person_1 (PATIENT): Ja, fair. Can we wrap this up? I've got a site meeting, and it's really not a big thing.

[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): This looks like an acute gout flare in the big toe joint. The knock is on my mind, and I can't fully exclude that it irritated the joint, but the heat, the redness and the way it came up overnight are much more gout than a bruise.
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'd like to start naproxen, five hundred milligrams twice a day with food, for five days.
[SEG0047] person_1 (PATIENT): Those anti-inflammatories, hey. Years ago I took Voltaren for my back and my stomach was on fire for days. I'd rather not do that again.
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, that changes things. I'm not going to give you the naproxen. With that stomach reaction we'll use colchicine instead.
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): Colchicine one milligram twice a day... no, sorry, too high. Five hundred micrograms twice a day, by mouth, for three days. If you get bad diarrhoea, stop and phone us.
[SEG0050] person_1 (PATIENT): Only three days? Good. And I still take the water tablet, ja? I'm not dropping that.

[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): Keep the hydrochlorothiazide every morning, same as usual. Colchicine is just for this flare. Skip the beer this weekend, the Saturday six-pack included, while the toe is this angry. Rest the foot up at home, and don't force a shoe on.
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): I want a uric acid blood test as well. Pop down to the path lab today before you head out; I need the level, even though it won't change this script.
[SEG0053] person_1 (PATIENT): Today, hey. Ok, if they're still open this side. Do I have to come back for the result, or will you phone?

[SEG0054] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come back here in a week and we'll go through the result and check the toe. If it's not settling in three days, or the redness spreads or you get a fever, come sooner, don't wait out the week.
